Mean and Variance of Continuous Distributions

Source: R/mcontinuous.R
cont.moments.Rd

Computes the mean and variance of common continuous distributions given their parameters.

mnorm(mean, sd)

mexp(rate)

mgamma(shape, rate)

mlnorm(meanlog, sdlog)

mbeta(shape1, shape2)

mchisq(df)

mt(df)

mf(df1, df2)

mtri(min = 0, max = 1, mode = 0.5)

Arguments

mean

mean of the normal distribution.

sd

standard deviation of the normal distribution.

rate

rate parameter (1/mean) of the exponential distribution.

shape,

rate shape and scale parameters of the gamma and beta distributions.

meanlog, sdlog

mean and standard deviation on the log scale (log-normal distribution).

shape1, shape2

shape parameters of the beta distribution (\(\alpha\) and \(\beta\)).

df

degrees of freedom (chi-squared and t-distribution).

df1, df2

numerator and denominator degrees of freedom (F-distribution).

min

lower limit of the triangular distribution.

max

upper limit of the triangular distribution.

mode

mode of the triangular distribution.

Value

A named numeric vector with elements mean and variance. Returns NA where moments do not exist.

Details

Normal:
\(\mu = \mu\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = \sigma^2\)

Exponential:
\(\mu = \frac{1}{\lambda}\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = \frac{1}{\lambda^2}\)

Gamma:
\(\mu = \frac{\alpha}{\beta}\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = \frac{\alpha}{\beta^2}\)

Log-Normal:
\(\mu = \exp(\mu_{log} + \frac{1}{2}\sigma_{log}^2)\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = (\exp(\sigma_{log}^2) - 1) \cdot \exp(2\mu_{log} + \sigma_{log}^2)\)

Beta:
\(\mu = \frac{\alpha}{\alpha + \beta}\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = \frac{\alpha\beta}{(\alpha+\beta)^2(\alpha+\beta+1)}\)

Chi-Squared:
\(\mu = \nu\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = 2\nu\)

t-Distribution:
\(\mu = 0 \quad (\nu > 1)\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = \frac{\nu}{\nu-2} \quad (\nu > 2)\)

F-Distribution:
\(\mu = \frac{n_2}{n_2-2} \quad (n_2 > 2)\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = \frac{2n_2^2(n_1+n_2-2)}{n_1(n_2-2)^2(n_2-4)} \quad (n_2 > 4)\)

Triangular:
\(\mu = \frac{a + b + c}{3}\)
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = \frac{a^2 + b^2 + c^2 - ab - ac - bc}{18}\)
where \(a\) = min, \(b\) = max and \(c\) = mode.

References

Casella, G. and Berger, R. L. (2002) Statistical Inference. Duxbury.

Johnson, N. L., Kotz, S. and Balakrishnan, N. (1994) Continuous Univariate Distributions, Vol. 1. Wiley.

Johnson, N. L., Kotz, S. and Balakrishnan, N. (1995) Continuous Univariate Distributions, Vol. 2. Wiley.

See also

dnorm, dexp, dgamma, dlnorm, dbeta, dchisq, dt, df

Examples

mnorm(mean = 0, sd = 1)
#>     mean variance 
#>        0        1 
mexp(rate = 0.5)
#>     mean variance 
#>        2        4 
mgamma(shape = 2, rate = 0.5)
#>     mean variance 
#>        4        8 
mlnorm(meanlog = 0, sdlog = 1)
#>     mean variance 
#> 1.648721 4.670774 
mbeta(shape1 = 2, shape2 = 3)
#>     mean variance 
#>     0.40     0.04 
mchisq(df = 4)
#>     mean variance 
#>        4        8 
mt(df = 5)
#>     mean variance 
#> 0.000000 1.666667 
mf(df1 = 5, df2 = 10)
#>     mean variance 
#> 1.250000 1.354167 
mtri(min = 0, max = 1, mode = 0.5)
#>       mean   variance 
#> 0.50000000 0.04166667 
mtri(min = 2, max = 10, mode = 4)
#>     mean variance 
#> 5.333333 2.888889
